mainTopic: The חורבן story: from בר קמצא's revenge through the siege and famine to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's escape to אספסיינוס
overview: This amud continues the famous אגדתא about the חורבן. The host throws בר קמצא out of the feast, and because the רבנן stayed silent, he informs on the Jews to the קיסר. He secretly puts a מום on the קרבן sent as a test, and רבי זכריה בן אבקולס blocks both plans to save the situation. רבי יוחנן says this caution destroyed the בית המקדש. Rome sends נירון, who sees signs that the city will fall, so he flees and converts, and רבי מאיר descends from him. אספסיינוס then besieges ירושלים, and the city has enough food for twenty-one years from three rich men. But the בריוני burn the stores to force a war, and a terrible famine follows, shown through the death of מרתא בת בייתוס. Finally, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי fakes his death to escape the city and greets אספסיינוס as king. His answer to the general's charges continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The host refuses every offer and throws בר קמצא out
steps.stepSummary: בר קמצא offers to pay for half the feast, then for the whole feast. The host keeps saying no, then physically takes him out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. He said to him: I will give you the cost of half your feast! He said to him: No. He said to him: I will give you the cost of your entire feast! He said to him: No. He took him by his hand, stood him up, and threw him out.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. בר קמצא keeps raising his offer so he will not be shamed, and the host keeps refusing. In the end the host removes him by force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offers go up step by step, from half the feast to the whole feast, and the answer is always the same short 'לא'. This shows how fixed the host's hatred is. Being physically walked out in front of everyone is the public shame that drives the rest of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: The money value of, the cost of
He took him out, threw him out

phrases.english: He said to him: No.
He said to him: I will give you
the cost of half your feast!
He said to him: No.
He said to him: I will give you
the cost of your entire feast!
He said to him: No.
He took him by his hand, stood him up, and threw him out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יָהֵיבְנָא לָךְ דְּמֵי פַּלְגָא דִּסְעוֹדְתָּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the previous part of the daf, where בר קמצא was found at the feast and told to leave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The host refuses all of בר קמצא's offers and publicly throws him out of the feast.

steps.title: בר קמצא blames the silent רבנן and decides to inform
steps.stepSummary: בר קמצא concludes that the רבנן who watched and did not protest must have approved, so he decides to slander them to the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Since the רבנן were sitting there and did not protest, learn from this that it was fine with them. I will go and inform on them to the king.
steps.whatsHappening: Now בר קמצא reacts. He is angry at the רבנן who saw the whole thing and stayed quiet, and he decides to get revenge by informing on them to the government.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His anger moves from the host to the רבנן. He reasons that their silence means they agreed with the host. This turns a private fight into a danger for the whole Jewish people.

keyTerms.meaning: It was fine with them, they were content
To slander, to inform on someone

steps.whyThisMatters: The story points to staying silent when someone is shamed as a link in the chain that led to the חורבן.

phrases.english: He said: Since the Sages were sitting there
and did not protest against him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the host. The רבנן did not stop him from shaming בר קמצא.

phrases.english: learn from it that they were content with it,

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזִיל אֵיכוֹל בְּהוּ קוּרְצָא בֵּי מַלְכָּא.
phrases.english: I will go and inform on them to the king.
phrases.notes: Literally 'eat their pieces' in the king's house. It's an Aramaic way of saying to slander someone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וַהֲווֹ יָתְבִי רַבָּנַן וְלָא מַחוֹ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how בר קמצא reacts to being thrown out in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר קמצא takes the רבנן's silence as approval and decides to inform on them.

steps.title: בר קמצא accuses the Jews and proposes a test
steps.stepSummary: בר קמצא tells the קיסר that the Jews rebelled. When asked for proof, he suggests sending them a קרבן to see whether they will offer it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and said to the emperor: The Jews have rebelled against you! He said to him: Who says so? He said to him: Send them an offering and see whether they sacrifice it.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קמצא carries out his plan and accuses the Jews of rebellion. The emperor asks for proof, and בר קמצא sets up a 'loyalty test' with a קרבן. This sets up the trick in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The emperor does not simply believe him, so בר קמצא needs a test he can control. Accepting a קרבן sent by the ruler would show loyalty, so refusing it would look like rebellion.

keyTerms.meaning: Who says so? What is the proof?

phrases.english: He went and said to the emperor:
The Jews have rebelled against you!
He said to him: Who says so?
He said to him: Send them an offering,
and see whether they sacrifice it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְקֵיסָר: מְרַדוּ בָּךְ יְהוּדָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the decision to inform that בר קמצא made in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר קמצא accuses the Jews of rebellion and sets up the test of the קרבן.

steps.title: The calf is sent and בר קמצא secretly blemishes it
steps.stepSummary: The emperor sends a three-year-old calf. On the way, בר קמצא makes a מום on its upper lip, or on its eyelids according to another version. That spot counts as a מום for Jews but not for the Romans.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and sent with him a three-year-old calf. While he was coming, he made a blemish on its upper lip, and some say on the eyelids. That is a place where for us it is a blemish, but for them it is not a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The emperor agrees to the test. בר קמצא then quietly damages the animal, so the Jews will have to refuse it while the Romans will think it is perfectly fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trick depends on the difference between Jewish law and Roman practice. Under הלכה the animal now cannot go on the מזבח, but the Romans see no defect. So the כהנים' refusal will look like rebellion. The גמרא brings two versions of where the מום was, and both are spots that fit this plan.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח
The eyelids, the thin parts of the eye

steps.confusionAlert: The calf is not blemished in the eyes of the Romans. That is the whole trap: the Jews must refuse it by הלכה, and the Romans see the refusal as an insult.

phrases.english: He went and sent with him a three-year-old calf.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the emperor and 'with him' means with בר קמצא.

phrases.english: While he was coming
he made a blemish on it, on the upper lip,
and some say on the eyelids –
a place where for us it is a blemish,
but for them it is not a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּהֲדֵי דְּקָאָתֵי שְׁדָא בֵּיהּ מוּמָא בְּנִיב שְׂפָתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the test proposed in step 3 and adds בר קמצא's sabotage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר קמצא puts a מום on the קרבן that is a defect under הלכה but not under Roman rules.

steps.title: The רבנן consider offering the blemished calf
steps.stepSummary: Because of the danger from the government, the רבנן think about offering the animal despite the מום, for the sake of שלום מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן thought to sacrifice it because of peace with the government.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן suggest a first way out: offer the animal anyway to keep peace with Rome. This sets up רבי זכריה's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן weigh the danger of angering the empire against the איסור of offering a בעל מום. Their idea is to let שלום מלכות outweigh the normal rule in this emergency.

keyTerms.meaning: To offer it as a sacrifice

phrases.english: The Sages thought to sacrifice it
because of peace with the government.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבוּר רַבָּנַן לְקָרוֹבֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם שְׁלוֹם מַלְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the problem created by the blemished calf in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן lean toward offering the blemished animal for the sake of שלום מלכות.

steps.title: רבי זכריה objects: people will think blemished animals are allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכריה בן אבקולס argues that if they offer it, people will wrongly learn that בעלי מומין may be brought on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זכריה בן אבקולס said to them: People will say that blemished animals may be offered on the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זכריה pushes back against the רבנן's plan. He worries that people who see it will learn the wrong הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His concern is not only the איסור in this one case. He is worried that the public will draw a false general rule from what they see. Because of this objection, the first plan is dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכם who objects to both plans
People will say (they will draw the wrong conclusion)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן אַבְקוּלָס:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zekharya ben Avkolas said to them:
People will say that blemished animals
may be offered on the altar!

steps.triggerLanguage: יֹאמְרוּ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין קְרֵיבִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the plan proposed in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's plan to offer the blemished animal for the sake of שלום מלכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Offering it publicly would teach people a false הלכה, that blemished animals are fit for the מזבח.

steps.title: The רבנן consider killing בר קמצא
steps.stepSummary: Since they cannot offer the calf, the רבנן think about killing בר קמצא so that he cannot go and report to the emperor.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought to kill him, so that he would not go and tell.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן suggest a second way out: stop the informer before he can report. This sets up רבי זכריה's second objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the first plan blocked, the danger now comes from בר קמצא's report. The new idea targets the informer himself instead of the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: So that he would not go and tell

phrases.english: They thought to kill him,
so that he would not go and tell.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבוּר לְמִיקְטְלֵיהּ דְּלָא לֵיזִיל וְלֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 6 blocks the first plan, the רבנן offer a different solution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן consider killing בר קמצא to stop him from informing.

steps.title: רבי זכריה objects: people will think blemishing קדשים is a capital crime
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכריה argues that killing בר קמצא would make people think that someone who puts a מום on קדשים deserves death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זכריה said to them: People will say that one who puts a blemish on קדשים is to be killed!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זכריה blocks the second plan too, again because people would learn the wrong הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a מום on קדשים is forbidden, but it is not punished by death. If they kill him, the public will think it is. So both plans fall for the same kind of reason: fear of teaching a false הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who puts a blemish on an animal
Sacred animals set aside as קרבנות

steps.whatToRemember: Both plans of the רבנן, offering the calf and killing בר קמצא, are blocked by רבי זכריה בן אבקולס for one reason: people would learn a false הלכה from what they saw.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zekharya said to them:
People will say that one who puts a blemish on sacred animals
is to be killed!

steps.triggerLanguage: יֹאמְרוּ מֵטִיל מוּם בַּקֳּדָשִׁים יֵהָרֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the plan proposed in step 7, in the same way that step 6 objected to step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's plan to kill בר קמצא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Killing him would teach people a false הלכה, that blemishing קדשים is punished by death.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן blames רבי זכריה's caution for the destruction
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the 'humility' of רבי זכריה בן אבקולס destroyed the בית המקדש, burned the היכל, and sent us into exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: The humility of רבי זכריה בן אבקולס destroyed our House, burned our היכל, and exiled us from our land.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן stops the story to judge what just happened. He says רבי זכריה's refusal to act led to the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 6 and 8, רבי זכריה blocked both ways of saving the situation because he worried people would learn the wrong הלכה. רבי יוחנן says this caution, which he calls עניוותנות, had terrible results: the בית המקדש was destroyed, the היכל was burned, and we went into exile.

keyTerms.meaning: humility; here it means being too cautious and holding back from acting
the Sanctuary, the main building of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says the destruction came because רבי זכריה would not act, not only because of the evil of בר קמצא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Humility' here is not praise. רבי יוחנן is criticizing a holding back that turned out to be a disaster.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that being too careful about how people might misread a decision can sometimes cause far greater damage.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: עִנְוְותָנוּתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן אַבְקוּלָס,
phrases.english: The humility of Rabbi Zecharya ben Avkolas
phrases.notes: He is talking about רבי זכריה holding back in steps 6 and 8, when he blocked both plans.

phrases.english: destroyed our House,
burned our Sanctuary,
and exiled us from our land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עִנְוְותָנוּתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן אַבְקוּלָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Judges the outcome of רבי זכריה's two objections.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זכריה's excessive caution caused the חורבן and the exile.

steps.title: נירון is sent and every arrow lands in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: Rome sends נירון קיסר. He shoots arrows in every direction, and each one falls in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent נירון קיסר against them. As he was coming, he shot an arrow to the east, and it fell in ירושלים. To the west, and it fell in ירושלים. To all four directions, and it fell in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: בר קמצא's report works, and Rome sends נירון קיסר to attack. נירון tests his fate with arrows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No matter which way נירון shoots, the arrow lands in ירושלים. This looks like a sign from heaven that the city will fall. It also sets up נירון's second test in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the four directions of the sky

phrases.english: They sent Nero Caesar against them.
When he was coming,
he shot an arrow to the east,
phrases.notes: He is looking for a sign about whether he will succeed.

phrases.english: and it came and fell in Jerusalem.
To the west, and it came and fell in Jerusalem.
To all four directions of the heavens,
and it came and fell in Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁדַּר עִלָּוַיְיהוּ לְנֵירוֹן קֵיסָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יוחנן's comment in step 9, the story resumes: the רבנן did nothing (steps 6–8), the test from step 3 made the Jews look rebellious, and Rome sends an army.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every arrow נירון shoots lands in ירושלים, a sign of the coming destruction.

steps.title: A child's פסוק makes נירון flee and convert
steps.stepSummary: A child tells נירון a פסוק about vengeance on אדום. נירון realizes he will be punished, runs away, converts, and רבי מאיר descends from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to a child: Tell me your verse. He said: 'And I will lay My vengeance upon אדום by the hand of My people ישראל.' נירון said: God wants to destroy His House and wipe His hands on that man (me). He fled, converted, and רבי מאיר came from him.
steps.whatsHappening: נירון does a second test by asking a child for the פסוק he learned. The answer frightens him so much that he abandons the mission and becomes a גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rome is connected to אדום. נירון understands that God will let him destroy the בית המקדש but will punish him for it afterward. So he refuses to be the tool, and amazingly, רבי מאיר comes from his descendants.

keyTerms.meaning: tell me your verse, meaning the one you just learned
Edom, the nation linked to Rome
to wipe His hands, meaning to punish the one used as the tool

phrases.english: He said to a child:
Tell me your verse.
He said to him:
"And I will lay My vengeance upon Edom
by the hand of My people Israel, etc."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בָּעֵי לַחֲרוֹבֵי בֵּיתֵיהּ,
phrases.english: He said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, wants to destroy His House,
and He wants to wipe His hands on that man.
phrases.notes: 'That man' is נירון talking about himself. He would be the one punished afterward.

phrases.english: He fled, went, and converted,
and Rabbi Meir descended from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְיָנוֹקָא: פְּסוֹק לִי פְּסוּקָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second test by נירון that settles his decision.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נירון refuses to be God's tool for the חורבן, converts, and becomes an ancestor of רבי מאיר.

steps.title: אספסיינוס besieges ירושלים, and three rich men are introduced
steps.stepSummary: Rome sends אספסיינוס קיסר, who besieges ירושלים for three years. Three wealthy men live in the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent אספסיינוס קיסר against them. He came and besieged the city for three years. There were three wealthy men in it: נקדימון בן גוריון, בן כלבא שבוע, and בן ציצית הכסת.
steps.whatsHappening: With נירון gone, Rome sends a new general who besieges the city. The גמרא introduces three rich men, setting up their role later in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The siege is a new stage of the story. The three wealthy men are named here so the גמרא can explain their names next and later tell how they tried to keep the city alive.

phrases.english: They sent Vespasian Caesar against them.
He came and besieged it for three years.
There were in it these three wealthy men:
Nakdimon ben Guryon,
and ben Kalba Savua,
and ben Tzitzit HaKesat.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁדְּרֵיהּ עִילָּוַיְיהוּ לְאַסְפַּסְיָינוּס קֵיסָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After נירון flees, Rome sends a replacement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אספסיינוס besieges ירושלים for three years. Three wealthy men are in the city.

steps.title: Explaining the names of the three rich men
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains each name: the sun shone for נקדימון, hungry guests left בן כלבא שבוע full, and בן ציצית הכסת's ציצית dragged on blankets. Another opinion says his seat was among Rome's nobles.
steps.simpleTranslation: נקדימון בן גוריון, because the sun shone for his sake. בן כלבא שבוע, because anyone who came into his house hungry as a dog left full. בן ציצית הכסת, because his ציצית dragged on blankets. Some say: because his seat was set among the great men of Rome.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain where each rich man's name comes from. For the third name it gives two explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is a wordplay: נקד sounds like 'shone', כלבא is 'dog' and שבוע is 'full', and כסת is 'blanket' or 'seat'. The איכא דאמרי reads כסת as his seat among Roman nobles instead of blankets under his feet.

keyTerms.meaning: shone, a play on the name נקדימון
a blanket or cushion; in the second explanation, a seat

phrases.aramaic: נַקְדִּימוֹן בֶּן גּוּרְיוֹן – שֶׁנָּקְדָה לוֹ חַמָּה בַּעֲבוּרוֹ.
phrases.english: Nakdimon ben Guryon, because the sun shone for his sake.
Ben Kalba Savua,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל הַנִּכְנָס לְבֵיתוֹ כְּשֶׁהוּא רָעֵב כְּכֶלֶב,
phrases.english: because anyone who entered his house hungry as a dog
would leave full.
Ben Tzitzit HaKesat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיְתָה צִיצָתוֹ נִגְרֶרֶת עַל גַּבֵּי כְּסָתוֹת.
phrases.english: because his tzitzit dragged on top of blankets.
phrases.notes: He means blankets were laid under him so he did not walk on the bare ground.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיְתָה כִּסְתּוֹ מוּטֶּלֶת בֵּין גְּדוֹלֵי רוֹמִי.
phrases.english: that his seat was placed among the great men of Rome.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַקְדִּימוֹן בֶּן גּוּרְיוֹן – שֶׁנָּקְדָה לוֹ חַמָּה בַּעֲבוּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the names introduced in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each rich man's name reflects his greatness. There are two explanations of the name בן ציצית הכסת.

steps.title: The three rich men offer supplies
steps.stepSummary: Each of the three wealthy men offers one type of supply for the besieged city: grain, wine/salt/oil, or wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: One said: I will feed them with wheat and barley. Another said: with wine, salt and oil. The third said: with wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The three rich men from the last step each promise to supply the city with something different during the siege.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 explained why each man got his name. Now we see what each one actually gave. Together they cover food, cooking basics, and fuel, which sets up the praise for the wood in the next step.

phrases.english: One said to them:
I will feed them with wheat and barley,
And one said to them:
With wine, and with salt, and oil,
And one said to them: With wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲנָא זָיֵינָּא לְהוּ בְּחִיטֵּי וּשְׂעָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the description of the three rich men by telling us what each one gave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three rich men split the job of supplying the city: grain, wine/salt/oil, and wood.

steps.title: The רבנן praise the gift of wood
steps.stepSummary: רבנן gave special praise to the man who supplied the wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן praised the one who gave the wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a comment: of the three gifts, רבנן praised the wood the most. This sets up the next step, which explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood sounds like the least important gift, so the praise is surprising. The גמרא will now show that fuel was actually the most valuable of the three.

phrases.english: And the Sages praised the one with the wood,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשַׁבַּחוּ רַבָּנַן לִדְצִיבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks out one of the three gifts from step 14 for special praise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gift of wood was the most praiseworthy.

steps.title: Why wood is so valuable: רב חסדא's keys
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא kept only the key to his woodshed for himself, because one storehouse of wheat needs sixty storehouses of wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב חסדא used to give all his keys to his servant except the key to the wood. As רב חסדא said: one storehouse of wheat needs sixty storehouses of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the praise for wood with what רב חסדא did and what he said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא trusted his servant with everything except the firewood, which shows he valued it most. His statement gives the reason: you need far more wood than wheat to cook and bake. So without the wood, the grain would have been almost useless.

phrases.english: For Rav Chisda, all the keys
he would hand over to his servant,
except for the one for the wood.
As Rav Chisda said:
One storehouse of wheat
requires sixty storehouses of wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַב חִסְדָּא כֹּל אַקְלִידֵי הֲוָה מָסַר לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the praise of wood from step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That the gift of wood was the most valuable of the three.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's habit of keeping the woodshed key, and his statement that wheat needs sixty times as much wood.

steps.title: Enough supplies for twenty-one years
steps.stepSummary: Together, the three men had enough to feed the city for twenty-one years.
steps.simpleTranslation: They had enough to feed the city for twenty-one years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up how much the three men had: enough to outlast the siege many times over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The siege lasted three years (step 12), and there was food for twenty-one. So hunger should never have been a problem. This makes the coming disaster something the people brought on themselves.
steps.whatToRemember: The city had plenty of food. The famine that follows was not caused by the siege itself.

phrases.english: They had enough to feed
for twenty-one years.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה לְהוּ לְמֵיזַן עֶשְׂרִים וְחַד שַׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the section on the three rich men's supplies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The supplies could have lasted twenty-one years.

steps.title: The zealots and the Sages disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבנן want to make peace with Rome, but the בריוני refuse. The בריוני want to fight, but רבנן say it will fail.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were בריוני among them. The רבנן said: Let us go out and make peace with them. The בריוני did not let them. The בריוני said: Let us go out and fight them. The רבנן said: It will not succeed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new group enters the story: the zealots inside ירושלים. They and רבנן block each other's plans, which sets up what the zealots do next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side vetoes the other: no peace and no battle. So the city just stays under siege, living on its stores. The zealots will now try to force a battle.

phrases.english: There were among them certain zealots,
The Sages said to them:
Let us go out and make peace with them.
They did not let them.
They said to them:
Let us go out and make battle with them,
The Sages said to them:
The matter will not succeed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲווֹ בְּהוּ הָנְהוּ בִּרְיוֹנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the supplies to the political conflict inside the city.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The zealots blocked peace, and רבנן rejected battle.

steps.title: The zealots burn the storehouses
steps.stepSummary: The בריוני burn the wheat and barley storehouses, and a famine breaks out.
steps.simpleTranslation: They got up and burned those storehouses of wheat and barley, and there was a famine.
steps.whatsHappening: To push the city into fighting, the zealots destroy the food supply, and the city starves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twenty-one years of food from step 17 are wiped out by the city's own people. The famine is their doing, not Rome's.
steps.whatToRemember: The famine in ירושלים came from the zealots burning the city's own food.

phrases.english: They arose and burned
those storehouses of wheat and barley,
and there was a famine.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָמוּ קְלֹנְהוּ לְהָנְהוּ אַמְבָּרֵי דְּחִיטֵּי וּשְׂעָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: What the zealots did after רבנן refused to fight.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The zealots' burning of the grain caused the famine.

steps.title: מרתא בת בייתוס tries to buy flour
steps.stepSummary: The rich מרתא בת בייתוס sends her messenger for flour four times. Each time, the kind she asked for is sold out before he gets there.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרתא בת בייתוס was one of the rich women of ירושלים. She sent her messenger for fine flour, but by the time he went it was sold. He offered ordinary flour; she said bring it, but it was sold too. Then coarse flour, then barley flour, and each time it was sold before he arrived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to show how bad the famine was: even a very rich woman cannot buy any flour at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flour gets worse each round: fine, ordinary, coarse, then barley. Every time, she agrees to the lower kind, and every time it is gone. Money no longer helps.

phrases.english: Marta bat Baitos
was one of the wealthy women of Jerusalem.
She sent her messenger,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: זִיל אַיְיתִי לִי סְמִידָא.
phrases.english: and said to him: Go bring me fine flour.
By the time he went, it was sold.
He came and said to her:
There is no fine flour, there is ordinary flour.
She said to him: Go bring me some.
By the time he went, it was sold.
He came and said to her:
There is no ordinary flour, there is coarse flour.
She said to him: Go bring me some.
By the time he went, it was sold.
He came and said to her:
There is no coarse flour, there is barley flour.
She said to him: Go bring me some.
By the time he went, it was sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָרְתָּא בַּת בַּיְיתּוֹס עַתִּירְתָּא דִּירוּשָׁלַיִם הַוְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the famine from step 19 through one person's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the famine, even the richest could not buy any flour.

steps.title: מרתא בת בייתוס goes out and dies
steps.stepSummary: Barefoot, מרתא goes out herself to find food. Dung sticks to her foot, and she dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: She had taken off her shoes. She said: I will go out and see if I can find something to eat. Dung stuck to her foot, and she died.
steps.whatsHappening: With nothing left to send for, מרתא goes out herself. A small disgusting thing happens, and she dies from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She goes out without even putting her shoes back on, which shows how desperate she was. A woman used to great luxury could not survive the shock of stepping in dung. The story ends the famine scene on a very sad note.
steps.whatToRemember: The famine was so bad that one of the wealthiest women in ירושלים went out barefoot looking for food and died.

phrases.english: She had her shoes removed,
She said: I will go out and see
if I can find something to eat.
Dung stuck to her foot,
and she died.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה שְׁלִיפָא מְסָאנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story of מרתא בת בייתוס from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרתא בת בייתוס died after going out barefoot to look for food.

steps.title: A verse about the delicate woman
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי reads a curse-פסוק about a pampered woman as describing מרתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי read this verse about her: 'The tender and delicate woman among you, who would not try to set the sole of her foot on the ground.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי reacts to מרתא's death by quoting a פסוק from the curses in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse describes a woman so pampered that she never put her bare foot on the ground. מרתא died exactly because she went out barefoot, so the curse came true in her.

phrases.aramaic: קָרֵי עֲלַהּ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai read concerning her:
"The tender and delicate woman among you
who would not try to set the sole of her foot" [on the ground].

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרֵי עֲלַהּ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's comment on מרתא's death from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרתא's death fulfills the curse of the pampered woman in דברים.

steps.title: Another version: the fig of רבי צדוק
steps.stepSummary: Some say מרתא died after eating one of רבי צדוק's sucked-out figs and feeling disgusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say she ate a dried fig of רבי צדוק, felt disgusted, and died. רבי צדוק had fasted for forty years so that ירושלים would not be destroyed. He was so thin that when he ate something, you could see it from the outside. When he ate to regain strength, they brought him dried figs. He sucked out the juice and threw the rest away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different account of how מרתא died. In this version she ate a leftover fig, not stepped in dung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fig had already been sucked dry by רבי צדוק and thrown away. מרתא was starving and ate it, but she was so used to luxury that the disgust killed her. Along the way, the גמרא tells us about רבי צדוק's forty years of fasting for ירושלים.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
she ate a dried fig of Rabbi Tzadok,
and became disgusted and died.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק יְתֵיב אַרְבְּעִין שְׁנִין בְּתַעֲנִיתָא
phrases.english: For Rabbi Tzadok sat forty years in fasting
so that Jerusalem would not be destroyed,
[so thin that] when he ate something
it could be seen from the outside.
And when he would eat [to regain strength],
phrases.notes: בריא here means eating to rebuild strength after fasting, not being healthy.

phrases.english: they would bring him dried figs,
he would suck out their juice and throw them away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of the death told in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Another tradition says מרתא died of disgust after eating a fig that רבי צדוק had already sucked dry.

steps.title: מרתא throws her money into the street
steps.stepSummary: As she dies, מרתא throws all her gold and silver into the market, fulfilling a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As she was dying, she brought out all her gold and silver and threw it into the marketplace. She said: 'What do I need this for?' This is what the verse says: 'They shall throw their silver in the streets.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends מרתא's story with her final act. She throws away her money, and the גמרא shows that a פסוק described exactly this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her wealth could not buy her food during the famine, so it was worthless to her. The פסוק in יחזקאל predicted that money would be thrown away because it cannot save anyone in a time of disaster.

keyTerms.meaning: She was dying (her soul was departing)
And this is what is written

steps.whatToRemember: מרתא was one of the wealthiest women in ירושלים, but in the famine her money was useless. She died throwing it away.

phrases.english: When she was dying,
she took out all her gold and her silver
and threw it into the marketplace.
She said: What do I need this for!
And this is what is written:
"They shall throw their silver in the streets."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה קָא נִיחָא נַפְשַׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes מרתא's story with her last act and a supporting פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the famine, wealth was worthless, as the פסוק predicted.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי secretly confronts his nephew
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי secretly summons אבא סקרא, head of the בריוני, and asks how long they will starve the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא סקרא, the head of the zealots of ירושלים, was the son of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's sister. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי sent him a message: 'Come to me in secret.' He came. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said to him: 'How long will you go on like this, killing everyone with hunger?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meets in secret with his nephew, the leader of the בריוני, and blames him for the famine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family connection explains why the head of the בריוני would come at all. The meeting is secret because the other בריוני would see talking with רבנן as betrayal. The complaint points back to step 19, where the בריוני burned the food stores.

keyTerms.meaning: Abba Sikra, leader of the zealots

phrases.english: Abba Sikra, the head of the zealots of Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: בַּר אֲחָתֵיהּ דְּרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי הֲוָה.
phrases.english: was the son of the sister of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.
He sent [a message] to him:
phrases.notes: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי is the one sending for אבא סקרא.

phrases.english: Come to me in secret.
He came.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַד אֵימַת עָבְדִיתוּ הָכִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: Until when will you act this way,
and kill everyone with hunger?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא סִקְרָא רֵישׁ בִּרְיוֹנֵי דִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves מרתא's story and opens the story of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's escape.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי secretly confronts the leader of the בריוני about the famine they caused.

steps.title: אבא סקרא is trapped, so רבן יוחנן בן זכאי asks for a way out
steps.stepSummary: אבא סקרא says the בריוני would kill him if he objected. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי asks for a plan to leave the city instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא סקרא said: 'What can I do? If I say anything to them, they will kill me!' רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said: 'Find me a plan so that I can get out. Perhaps it will bring about a small rescue.'
steps.whatsHappening: אבא סקרא admits he cannot control his own men. So רבן יוחנן בן זכאי changes his request: he asks for help escaping the city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stopping the בריוני is impossible, so the goal shifts from saving the whole city to saving something. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי hopes that getting outside might bring a 'small rescue.' This sets up his later meeting with the Romans.

phrases.english: He said to him: What can I do,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי אָמֵינָא לְהוּ מִידֵּי קָטְלוּ לִי!
phrases.english: for if I say anything to them, they will kill me!
He said to him: Find me a plan
for me, so that I can get out;
perhaps there will be a small rescue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי אֶיעֱבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives אבא סקרא's reply and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's new request.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the בריוני cannot be stopped, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי seeks to leave the city to save what he can.

steps.title: The plan: fake a death
steps.stepSummary: אבא סקרא tells רבן יוחנן בן זכאי to pretend to be sick and then dead, and to have only his students carry him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'Pretend to be sick, and let everyone come and ask how you are. Then bring something rotten and put it next to you, so people will say you have died. Let your students carry you, and no one else, so that nobody notices you are light. They know that a living person is lighter than a dead one.'
steps.whatsHappening: אבא סקרא lays out the escape plan step by step. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי will fake illness and death, then be carried out in a coffin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the plan has a purpose. Visitors spread news of the illness, and the rotten smell makes the death believable. Only his students may carry the coffin, so that no outsider notices it is too light for a dead body.

phrases.english: He said to him: Pretend to be sick,
and let everyone come and ask about you,
and bring something rotten
and lay it next to you,
so they will say that you have died.
And let your students carry you,
and let no other person carry you,
so that they will not notice that you are light,
for they know that a living person is lighter than a dead one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נְקוֹט נַפְשָׁךְ בִּקְצִירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's request for an escape plan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The escape plan: fake illness and death, and have only the students carry the coffin so no one notices it is light.

steps.title: The students carry out the plan
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי follows אבא סקרא's plan, and רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע carry him, one on each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did so. רבי אליעזר took one side and רבי יהושע took the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: The plan from the last step is put into action. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי pretends to be dead, and his two top students carry him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא סקרא had said that only the students should carry him, so no one else could feel that he was light and still alive. Now we see exactly who those students were: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: He did so (he followed the plan)
Went in under it (took hold of it to carry it)

phrases.english: He did so.

phrases.aramaic: נִכְנַס בּוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִצַּד אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer went in to carry him on one side,
and Rabbi Yehoshua on the other side.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָבֵיד הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the plan אבא סקרא gave in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי is carried out as a 'dead man' by רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

steps.title: Getting past the guards at the gate
steps.stepSummary: The guards want to stab and then push the 'body', but אבא סקרא stops them both times, and the gate is opened.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they reached the gate, the guards wanted to stab him. He said to them: People will say, 'They stabbed their own רבי!' They wanted to push him. He said to them: People will say, 'They pushed their own רבי!' They opened the gate for him, and he went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The guards at the city gate try to test whether the body is really dead. אבא סקרא stops them by warning about how it would look.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stabbing or pushing would have shown that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was alive. אבא סקרא does not argue about the test itself. He argues about disgrace: people would say the zealots attack even their own רבי. That convinces the guards, and the escape works.

keyTerms.meaning: The entrance or gate (of the city)

phrases.english: When they reached the gate,
they wanted to stab him.
phrases.notes: 'They' here means the guards at the gate, the zealots who controlled the city.

phrases.english: He said to them: People will say, 'They stabbed their Rabbi!'
phrases.notes: The one speaking is אבא סקרא, the leader of the בריוני, who came along with them.

phrases.english: They wanted to push him.
He said to them: People will say, 'They pushed their Rabbi!'
They opened the gate for him, and he went out.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְטוֹ לְפִיתְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the escape: the plan is tested at the gate and succeeds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא סקרא stops the guards from testing the body, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי leaves the city.

steps.title: Greeting the Roman general as king
steps.stepSummary: When רבן יוחנן בן זכאי reaches the Roman camp, he greets אספסיינוס twice as 'king'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he got there, he said: Peace upon you, king! Peace upon you, king!
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי arrives at the Roman camp and greets אספסיינוס with the title 'king'. This sets up the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אספסיינוס is a general at this point, not the emperor. Calling him 'king' is surprising, and it leads straight into his angry reply in the next step.

phrases.english: When he got there,
he said: Peace upon you, king!
Peace upon you, king!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְטָא לְהָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the escape, the scene moves to the Roman camp.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי greets אספסיינוס as king.

steps.title: The general says he deserves two death penalties
steps.stepSummary: אספסיינוס says the greeting makes רבן יוחנן בן זכאי guilty either way: for calling a non-king 'king', or, if he is king, for not coming to him earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You deserve two death penalties. One, because I am not a king and you call me king. And also, if I am a king, why didn't you come to me until now?
steps.whatsHappening: אספסיינוס attacks the greeting from two directions. Either answer gets רבן יוחנן בן זכאי in trouble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is a trap. If he is not king, the greeting is treason against the real emperor. If he is king, then רבן יוחנן בן זכאי should have come out to him much sooner. The next step begins the answer to the first charge.

phrases.english: He said to him: You deserve two death penalties:
phrases.notes: The speaker is אספסיינוס. Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'death penalty.'

phrases.english: one, because I am not a king
and you call me king;
and also, if I am a king,

phrases.aramaic: עַד הָאִידָּנָא אַמַּאי לָא אָתֵית לְגַבַּאי.
phrases.english: why didn't you come to me until now?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיחַיְּיבַתְּ תְּרֵי קָטְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the 'king' greeting from step 30.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either he is not king, so the title is a crime, or he is king, so the delay in coming to him is a crime.

steps.title: Beginning to answer the first charge
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי starts to respond, quoting the first charge: 'I am not a king.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About what you said, 'I am not a king'...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי repeats the first charge so he can answer it, and his answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He handles the two charges one at a time, starting with the first. Here he only repeats the charge; his actual reply comes next.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רבן יוחנן בן זכאי is the one answering.

phrases.english: What you said, 'I am not a king'...

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּקָאָמְרַתְּ לָאו מַלְכָּא אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the reply to the first of the two charges in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Point-by-point reply, beginning with the first charge (continues on the next amud)
